newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN SHARES SET FOR FURTHER GAINS AFTER BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN SHARES SET FOR FURTHER GAINS AFTER BUDGET.

text.p: The Bel-20 index of leading shares is heading for further gains after a positive assessment of the country's 1997 budget by international players, dealers said on Wednesday.

"Foreign institutionals are giving the budget a positive reading and bonds are also reacting positively which further reduces long-term rates and the yield spread between Belgium and Germany," one dealer said.
At 0845 GMT, the Bel-20 was up 0.46 percent, or 8.10 points, at 1,787.26, with about 700 million francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
The Belgian government said Tuesday its 1997 budget would propel it into Europe's economic and monetary union in 1999.

The budget aims to cut the total public sector deficit to 2.9 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 1997, from an estimated 3.3 percent in 1996 through an austerity package worth 80 billion Belgian francs ($2.5 billion).
"Market sentiment is positive," one dealer said.
The retail sector was in the limelight with Delhaize and Colruyt among the early leading gainers.
Delhaize was up 2.0 percent at 1,820, mainly on the recent strong performance by U.S. unit Food Lion and a solid dollar.
Fellow retailer GIB, due to publish first-half 1996 earnings on Thursday, fared worse and dipped 0.2 percent to 1,300.
Analysts predict that losses at fast-food chain Quick would dampen the profit rise of parent GIB and counter the cost savings from GIB's GB supermarket restructuring.
Holding firm Societe Generale de Belgique did not budge following uneventful first-half earnings published after Tuesday's close and was steady at 2,465 francs.
